key_insight: SpikeDS uses dual sparsity—binary spikes plus window pruning—to make 3D MRI transformer inference more efficient for predicting perineural invasion in cholangiocarcinoma.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help identify PNI risk from volumetric MRI with lower compute and energy costs, supporting more practical deployment of AI imaging tools.
method: Dual Sparsity Spiking Attention (DSSA) combines activation sparsity with spatial sparsity.
Window-based Expert Mixture Spiking Attention (W-EMSA) attends only to salient windows based on firing rates.
Cross-Window Spiking Self-Attention (CW-SSA) lets pruned windows still provide key-value context for global information exchange.
evidence_signal: On 139 cholangiocarcinoma patients with 5-fold cross-validation, SpikeDS reached an AUC of 0.753 while using 14.4 mJ, outperforming the best baseline in both accuracy and energy efficiency.
watch_item: Performance was shown on a single clinical cohort, so broader validation and real-world robustness testing are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: SpikeDS: Dual Sparsity Spikformer for Perineural Invasion Prediction in 3D MRI
